items.informal_name: Weight Homomorphism on Single Finite Support Function
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} [inst : Semiring R] (w : σ → M) [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M]
  [inst_2 : Module R M] (s : σ) (r : R), (Finsupp.weight w) (Finsupp.single s r) = r • w s
items.informal_description: For any index $ s $ and scalar $ r $, the weighted sum homomorphism $ \text{weight}_w $ applied to the finite support function that assigns $ r $ to $ s $ and zero to all other indices equals $ r \cdot w(s) $.

items.informal_name: Sum of Single-Indexed Monomial in Monoid Algebra
items.type:
∀ {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {R : Type u_6} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid N] {m : M} {r : R}
  {h : M → R → N}, h m 0 = 0 → Finsupp.sum (MonoidAlgebra.single m r) h = h m r
items.informal_description: In a monoid algebra $ R[M] $ over a semiring $ R $ and an additive commutative monoid $ M $, for any monomial $ \text{single}_m(r) $ (which has coefficient $ r $ at $ m \in M $ and zero elsewhere), and for any function $ h : M \to R \to N $ into an additive commutative monoid $ N $ satisfying $ h(m, 0) = 0 $, the sum $ \sum h(m, r) $ over the monomial equals $ h(m, r) $. This follows because all terms in the monomial vanish except at $ m $, and the zero condition ensures no contribution from zero coefficients.

items.informal_name: Sum of Single Basis Element in Additive Monoid Algebra
items.type:
∀ {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {R : Type u_6} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid N] {m : M} {r : R}
  {h : M → R → N}, h m 0 = 0 → Finsupp.sum (AddMonoidAlgebra.single m r) h = h m r
items.informal_description: For any additive monoid $M$, semiring $R$, and function $h : M \times R \to N$ satisfying $h(m, 0) = 0$, the finite sum of the basis element $\text{single}_M(m, r)$ under $h$ evaluates to $h(m, r)$. This expresses that summing a formal $R$-linear combination with a single non-zero coefficient $r$ at $m$ reduces to evaluating $h$ at $(m, r)$.

items.informal_name: Weight Homomorphism on Single Index: $\text{weight}(\delta_s^c, f) = f(s) \cdot c$
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : Module R M]
  [inst_3 : DecidableEq σ] (s : σ) (c : M) (f : σ →₀ R), (Finsupp.weight (Pi.single s c)) f = f s • c
items.informal_description: For any index $ s \in \sigma $, element $ c \in M $, and finite support function $ f : \sigma \to_0 R $, the weighted sum homomorphism evaluated at the function $ \delta_s^c $ (which is $ c $ at $ s $ and zero elsewhere) applied to $ f $ equals $ f(s) \cdot c $. This expresses that the homomorphism acts as scalar multiplication at the specified index when restricted to single-index functions.

items.informal_name: Weight Homomorphism Applied to Single Index Function Yields Corresponding Vector
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : DecidableEq σ] (s : σ) (f : σ →₀ R),
  (Finsupp.weight (Pi.single s 1)) f = f s
items.informal_description: For any index $s$ in $\sigma$ and finite support function $f : \sigma \to_0 R$, applying the weight homomorphism to the function that is 1 at $s$ and 0 elsewhere results in $f(s)$. In symbols, $\text{weight}(\delta_s)(f) = f(s)$, where $\delta_s$ denotes the finite support function with $\delta_s(s) = 1$ and $\delta_s(i) = 0$ for $i \neq s$.

items.informal_name: Sum of Scalar Multiples with Single Non-Zero Component in a Module
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_3} [inst : DecidableEq ι] [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid α] {R : Type u_7}
  [inst_3 : Semiring R] [inst_4 : Module R α] (f : ι → α) (r : R) (i₀ : ι), ∑ i, Pi.single i₀ r i • f i = r • f i₀
items.informal_description: For a module $\alpha$ over a semiring $R$, given a function $f : \iota \to \alpha$, a scalar $r \in R$, and an index $i_0 \in \iota$, the sum over all indices $i$ of the scalar multiple $(\text{single}_{i_0}(r)) \cdot f(i)$ equals $r \cdot f(i_0)$. Here, $\text{single}_{i_0}(r)$ denotes the function in $\prod_{j : \iota} R$ that takes value $r$ at $i_0$ and $0$ elsewhere.
